messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident fired: PD#DB-4821 -> RedisPoolHighClients; severity: P1; triggered by redis.maxclients > 95% on prod-redis-cluster-03. Paging: alice_oncall. Details: https://pagerduty.example/INCIDENTS/DB-4821

pagerduty: page sent to alice_oncall at 2025-11-02T02:02:22Z; escalation policy: db-oncall -> db-escalation -> site-ops.

alice_oncall: acked. I'm on it. jumping into metrics now. @carla_pg and @dan_redis fyi.

alice_oncall: quick context: error spike on API write path (POST /v1/generate). Errors are Redis connection errors (EMFILE / maxclients). Grafana dashboards show connection count steady rising for 15m.

bob_sre: saw a correlated increase in pgbouncer wait_count and client timeouts around 01:47 UTC. Could be connection churn from a rollout.

carla_pg: no major DB CPU spike, PG replicas look fine. This smells like client-side leak or redis eviction pressure. Any recent deploys?

alice_oncall: deploy bot: deploy 2025-11-02T01:38 -> service inference-api:service-v5 rolled 1h ago. Rolling restart + feature flag for batching. Could have increased concurrent connections.

dan_redis: tailing redis logs now. Seeing many 'max number of clients reached' and a lot of slowlog entries for scripts. Also frequent EVALSHA calls.

alice_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) temp throttle upstream traffic via rate limiting rule for /v1/generate to 60% of baseline. 2) increase redis maxclients on prod-redis-cluster-03 from 10000 -> 15000 (requires restart of that node). 3) add short-lived pgbouncer tuning: increase pool_size and max_client_conn. 4) if needed, failover to read-only replica for non-write requests and roll back the batching change.

bob_sre: +1 on throttling. I'll put an ingress rule to apply iptables limit via our edge-proxy for the route. Doing now:```
# edgectl rate-limit set --route /v1/generate --percent 60 --reason "emergency db backpressure"
edgectl: applied
```

alice_oncall: dan, can you confirm whether increasing maxclients is safe without OOM? Which node is at risk?

dan_redis: node 03 is the hot one. Memory usage is at 72%—we have headroom. Increasing maxclients is just limits, but will raise file descriptors; need a short restart to apply sysctl on that instance. Recommend draining traffic from 03 first. I can failover replicas to promote 04 if necessary.

ops-bot: runbook snippet: "To temporarily reduce redis connections: 1) enable edge throttle; 2) apply pgbouncer graceful restart; 3) cycle redis node after draining clients; 4) monitor client reconnect rate."

alice_oncall: performing pgbouncer graceful restart on inference-pgbouncer pool now. Will sequence: restart pgbouncer on pool-1 -> wait 30s -> restart pool-2.

carla_pg: note: pgbouncer change may increase load on redis as clients reconnect; monitor for reconnection storms. Suggest increasing reconnect-backoff in client config if we see spikes.

bob_sre: pgbouncer restart done on pool-1. Wait 45s: wait_count dropping from 230 -> 90. 503 errors decreased by ~12%.

alice_oncall: starting edge throttle rule, applying now.

edgectl: rate limit applied at 2025-11-02T02:10:31Z.

alice_oncall: starting controlled drain of prod-redis-cluster-03. Marking 03 for draining clients.

dan_redis: running:```
# redis-cli -h redis-03 CLUSTER FAILOVER NO-ONE
# redis-cli -h redis-03 CONFIG SET maxclients 15000
# systemctl restart redis
```

dan_redis: drain initiated. Connections on 03 down from 9,800 -> 1,200 over 2m as clients reconnect to 04. Restarting redis-03 now.

ops-bot: automatic alert suppressed for 10m while manual remediation in progress (controlled by alice_oncall).

alice_oncall: restart complete. redis-03 back up and accepting clients. Observing connection spread more evenly across cluster. Slowlog counts decreasing.

emily_support: support check-in: apps report reduced 500s but a few customers still see intermittent 502. Logged affected customers: [acme-inc, betacorp, charlie-analytics]. Notifying them now with status update.

emily_support: posting customer-facing note: "We are experiencing elevated errors for some inference requests; mitigation underway; expected reduced errors within 30m. We will follow up with a post-incident summary."

bob_sre: metrics: redis.client_connections 1m avg went from 9.2k -> 6.3k after action. API 5xx rate down 78% relative to peak.

alice_oncall: removing edge throttle gradually: set to 80% now to avoid sudden spike. Will fully remove in 10m if stable.

edgectl: rate limit updated to 80% at 2025-11-02T02:28:54Z.

carla_pg: can we correlate the batching flag? If it increases concurrent client connections aggressively, we should revert. I propose feature-flag rollback if we see another spike after throttle removed.

alice_oncall: recorded rollback flag: feature.batch-mode -> off. Will hold as a canary disabled for 2h.

dan_redis: monitoring: no 'max number of clients' logs for 12m. slowlog tail shows scripts running but latency back to baseline.

alice_oncall: handing off to bob_sre for watch and postmortem. Handoff notes:
- incident id: PD#DB-4821
- root cause hypothesis: client churn from recent batching rollout caused connection pile-up -> pgbouncer wait queue -> redis maxclients saturation on node-03 (hot shard).
- actions taken: edge rate-limit (60% -> 80%), pgbouncer graceful restarts, drained + restarted redis-03, increased maxclients to 15000, feature-flag rollback for batching.
- customer impact: elevated 5xx for ~18m window; ~3% of total requests affected, 3 named customers reported.
- follow-ups: create postmortem, add automated health check to detect per-node connection skew, add deploy canary to limit connection growth, add reconnect-backoff client-side.

bob_sre: acked handoff. I'll keep watch for 1h and start postmortem doc. I'll also open an engineering task to add per-shard connection alerting and to add the deploy canary gate.

emily_support: will send a final update to affected customers after 30m.

pagerduty: incident resolved by alice_oncall at 2025-11-02T02:46:00Z; incident state: resolved.

alice_oncall: thanks team. tagging this as postmortem-needed and linking to ticket ENGOPS-1284.

ops-bot: Reminder: please run the post-incident checklist: add timeline, impact numbers, root cause analysis, and owner for follow-ups.

bob_sre: creating postmortem doc now: https://wiki.redwood/ENGOPS/DB-4821-postmortem

emily_support: sent customer follow-up. No escalations.

alice_oncall: closing thread; if any regressions pop up ping me or escalate to site-ops. :white_check_mark:
